messages:
maria: Quick question — can we make the gateway routing rule for header `x-model` support a soft fallback across model aliases? Customer wants requests pinned to `redwood/llama-70b:v2` but fall back to `v1` when v2 fails compatibility checks (e.g., >4k seq or missing kv-cache).

tamir: I think so. We already have alias resolution, but not compatibility-aware fallback. Would need a compatibility predicate on the route, plus ranking between pinned and fallback aliases.

aj: Important: how do we record telemetry? We need fallback counts per route, per alias, and token/cost deltas so SRE/customer can see impact. Also need an alert if fallback rate > 5%. :thinking: 

tom: Proposal: add `pin_mode` to route config with values `strict` | `soft` and a `compatibility` block. Example config:```json
{
  "match": {"header.x-model": "customer-preferred"},
  "pin_mode": "soft",
  "model_chain": ["redwood/llama-70b:v2", "redwood/llama-70b:v1"],
  "compatibility": {"max_input_length": 4096, "requires_kv_cache": true}
}
```

maria: That looks reasonable. For `soft` the gateway should try v2, run an async compatibility check (cheap heuristics) and if incompatible immediately route to next model in `model_chain` without failing the request. For `strict` it should return 4xx and log.

tamir: Implementation notes: runtime needs a fast capability matcher (model metadata cache) and a path that avoids extra RPC latency. We should avoid spinning up a warm attempt then falling back — instead consult metadata and cheap heuristics before scheduling.

aj: Console/telemetry UX: we should add a small panel on the route page showing last 7d fallback rate, average cost delta, and a top-5 input examples that triggered fallback (sanitized). Also expose an API to query fallback events for audits.

ops-bot: deploy: routing-service v1.12.3 -> canary started for cluster-us-east-1 at 2025-08-21T14:02:00Z

tom: One more edge: what if v2 is compatible but overloaded? Need capacity-aware fallback. Suggest a policy priority: compatibility -> quota/capacity -> cost preference. Include `allow_capacity_fallback: true` flag.

maria: Agreed. I'll draft an RFC with config schema, telemetry requirements, and rollout plan (canary -> 10% -> 100%). Will include example console wireframes for the route page.

aj: Thanks — please add a note about privacy for surfaced examples. Also add cost impact estimate for customers (show projected token cost if fallback occurs).

maria: Will do. Filing RFC: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RF-3141 (WIP).
